effects: Permanently cancels the signer's order with this UID by setting filledAmount[orderUid] to the max value. This blocks any later fill of an order signed off-chain or pre-signed. The call reverts unless the signer is the owner encoded in the UID.
No tokens, ETH or allowances move. The call is not payable.
formats.shown: "Cancel order" with the 56-byte order UID shown as raw hex.

findings.title: invalidateOrder: the order UID hides the order's terms (sell/buy token, amounts, receiver) that are being cancelled.
findings.evidence: GPv2Order.sol extractOrderUidParams: the UID is the packed orderDigest (32 bytes) + owner (20 bytes) + validTo (4 bytes). Descriptor field orderUid 'Order ID' format raw. Case 0 shows 0x3fae…6b36ec80.
findings.fix: No descriptor can decode the digest. Optionally, a note in the label that the ID stands for an order placed on Ophis.

findings.title: invalidateOrder: the order expiry inside the UID could be shown as a date with a slice.
findings.evidence: GPv2Order.sol extractOrderUidParams: validTo := shr(224, calldataload(add(orderUid.offset, 52))). The descriptor shows only the raw 56-byte orderUid.
findings.fix: Add a field with path orderUid.[52:56], format date (encoding timestamp), label 'Order expires'. That helps the signer recognise which order is being cancelled.

effects: If signed is true, the signer's order becomes executable (preSignature[orderUid] = PRE_SIGNED). Solvers can then settle it, pulling the order's sell token from the signer through the vault relayer allowance and paying the buy token to the order's receiver.
If signed is false, the pre-signature is cleared, so the order can no longer be settled through a pre-signature.
The call reverts unless the signer is the owner encoded in the UID. No tokens or ETH move in this call, and it is not payable.
formats.shown: The static intent "Authorize or revoke order", the raw order UID, and an 'Authorized' field reading true or false.

findings.title: setPreSignature: the static intent does not say whether this call authorizes or revokes the order.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "intent": "Authorize or revoke order", no interpolatedIntent. Only the 'Authorized' field (raw true/false) tells the direction. In GPv2Signing.sol setPreSignature, signed=true sets PRE_SIGNED and signed=false clears it. Cases 1 and 2 render the same intent for opposite actions.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent that carries the flag, e.g. "Set pre-signature of order {orderUid} to {signed}", or a clearer label such as 'Order can be executed' for signed.

findings.title: setPreSignature: authorizing makes an order executable whose sell amount, tokens and receiver are hidden behind the UID digest.
findings.evidence: GPv2Signing.sol setPreSignature stores PRE_SIGNED for orderUid. GPv2Order.sol extractOrderUidParams shows the UID packs only digest+owner+validTo. Descriptor field orderUid format raw.
findings.fix: Not decodable from calldata. Wallets should pair this with the order details from the Ophis API. Optionally show validTo via the orderUid.[52:56] date slice.

findings.title: setPreSignature: the order expiry packed in the UID is not shown, although a slice could extract it.
findings.evidence: GPv2Order.sol: validTo := shr(224, calldataload(add(orderUid.offset, 52))). The descriptor shows only the raw orderUid.
findings.fix: Add a field {path: orderUid.[52:56], format: date, params: {encoding: timestamp}, label: 'Valid until'}.
